title: Phone Slip: Rock River Gazette, "All Three Plants Shut Down"

fields.message: Says a source told him ALL 3 Ironcrest plants are shut down + customer data stolen in a ransomware attack. Wants an on-record comment. "If I don't hear back by eight, the story will say the company declined to comment." Email: newsdesk@rockrivergazette.example. CCO: Neither claim matches our fact sheet (plants running in manual mode, no customer data confirmed). 110-word holding stmt drafted. Need CEO OK + GC review. Can I say "cybersecurity incident"? "Ransomware"?

instructorNote: Misinformation test. Watch for the CEO to approve a short holding statement taken only from the fact sheet. It should say what is known, what is not known, what is being done and when the next update comes. It should correct the claim that all three plants are shut down without guessing about data theft. The GC should check that the wording, including whether to say "ransomware," matches the 8-K approach and the employee and dealer messages (ICMP 7, IDCCI 6). The MSEL row puts the call at 18:32, but the slip shows 4:02 PM so it stays consistent with the 16:05 clock. The reporter's 8:00 PM deadline still lands after the 19:00 Disclosure Committee.
